model: General insurer free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; attributable cash earnings after regulatory capital retention, net debt zero)
model_label: Insurer FCFE at cost of equity, component-built on net earned premium: insurance margin + shareholders'-funds income - interest - NCI leakage, taxed, less capital retained to grow the regulatory base. Hybrid of the SKILL.md insurer row and the operating-company engine; BVPS x exit-P/B cross-check in inputs.notes.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 NET EARNED PREMIUM (management P&L, FY26 AR line 5640). NOT the CSV 'revenue' column (18,666 = AASB 17 insurance revenue, gross of the 32.5% quota share) and NOT GWP (18,412): the insurance margin that management guides (FY27 14.5-16.5%) is stated on NEP, so NEP is the base the margin path multiplies. NEP grew 5.4% in FY26 against GWP +7.6% because the RACQI book was only in Group reinsurance from 1 Jan 2026.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,340m ordinary shares on issue at the 25 Aug 2026 final-dividend record date (20.0c = $468m, FY26 AR note 4.4) after the 27.3m-share $200m buyback completed 13 May 2026, plus 4m unvested share rights supported by treasury shares (note 4.3). Held FLAT: SBC (~$13m) is expensed inside the flows. The 159m 'dilutive potential shares' from Capital Notes 2/3 are EXCLUDED: they are Tier 1/Tier 2 capital instruments that convert at market price, and their finance cost ($56m post-tax FY26) is already charged in the flows as interest.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. The flow discounted is attributable profit AFTER the $190m interest line on IAG's $2,868m interest-bearing liabilities (Tier 2 subordinated notes and Capital Notes that are regulatory capital, not operating debt). Deducting them again would double-charge (SKILL.md: never subtract net debt from a post-interest flow). Cash of $2,047m sits inside the technical-reserve and shareholders'-funds portfolios whose income is inside the flows, so it is not added either. total_debt and cash below are audit-only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 free cash flow to equity: NPAT attributable 1,022 less capital retained 89 (= 1,022 - 733 dividends paid - 200 buyback). CET1 fell 3,939 -> 3,337 in FY26 because ~$600m of surplus funded the RACQI acquisition; that is M&A, not organic retention, and is not in the base flow.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: NPAT attributable to IAG shareholders FY2026 (cash earnings 1,025; the $3m difference is acquired-intangible amortisation). Statutory OCF (1,042) and FCF are unusable: the financial-parser could not separate capex from investment-portfolio purchases, and OCF swings with claims timing and reinsurance recoveries (FY16 -1,946; FY24 +1,800).
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments $13.2m FY26 ($11.3m FY25; FY26 AR line 12043, thousands) are expensed inside administration expense and the flow starts from profit AFTER that charge, so no second deduction is made and sbc is recorded as 0 in the flows. The 4m unvested rights are in the diluted count. House and street bases coincide (band collapsed).
inputs.interest_income_note: Investment income on shareholders' funds ($383m FY26, $403m FY25) and on technical reserves ($246m, inside insurance profit) is LEFT IN the flows because the matching assets are not added to equity value and no net debt is deducted (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction). The shareholders'-funds line is carried as its own component of the margin path.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-23T02:09:15Z (INTRADAY ASX print, 12:09 AEST, on the day the ACCC announced its Phase 2 opposition to the RAC Insurance acquisition; volatile, replace at the regular close). 52-week range 6.39-8.72.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-08-25 (dividend record date share count; balance-sheet equity 2026-06-30)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest and no debt is deducted. AUD 10-year government yield ~4.4% (Sept 2026, assumed) + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta 0.85 (large-cap domestic general insurer; low earnings beta to GDP, defensive demand) = 9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. Catastrophe and reserve volatility is charged in the bear scenario flows and its 25% weight, not stacked on the rate (charge risk once). One rate across all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease principal ($82m FY26) and interest are inside administration expense and therefore inside the insurance margin; lease liabilities ($375m) are not debt in the model (which carries none).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged IN THE FLOWS: non-controlling interests (RACV's 30% of Insurance Manufacturers of Australia, RACQ's 10% of RACQI) took $195m of FY26 post-tax profit (16.0%; FY25 $176m, 11.4%; FY24 $135m). Modelled as a 2.4%-of-NEP pre-tax-equivalent deduction from the margin path (FY26: 195/0.7/10,523 = 2.65%; FY25 2.52%; FY24 ~2.1%), so the taxed margin reproduces attributable NPAT. No separate bridge deduction.
inputs.tax_note: 30% Australian corporate rate applied to attributable pre-tax profit: FY26 effective 522/1,742 = 30.0%, FY25 30.6%, cash tax paid 474 (FY26) / 277 (FY25). No shelter, no ramp.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = NEP. ebitda_margin_path = attributable pre-tax profit / NEP = reported insurance margin (on NEP) + shareholders'-funds investment income % - interest % - fee-business/corporate % - NCI pre-tax-equivalent %. FY26 actual: 14.7 + 3.6 - 1.8 - 0.0 - 2.65 = 13.9% -> x0.70 = 1,024 vs NPAT 1,022. FY25 actual: 17.5 + 4.0 - 1.9 + 2.7 (BI release) - 2.5 = 19.8% -> 1,383 vs 1,359. da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation sits inside the expense ratio; cash earnings add back only $3m). capex_pct_path = equity retained to grow the regulatory capital base = ~0.35 x NEP growth (base): PCA is 27.9% of NEP (2,938/10,523) and CET1 target midpoint is 1.0x PCA, so each $1 of NEP growth needs ~$0.28 of retained CET1, lifted to ~0.35 for capital-intensity creep (rising perils allowances, APRA). At terminal 2.5% growth that is ~0.9% of NEP, ~9% of NPAT retained, consistent with a ~35% return on tangible equity (NPAT 1,022 / NTA 2,855). FCF out of the engine is therefore FCFE = attributable NPAT - growth capital.
inputs.notes: MODEL: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes an insurer to 'BVPS compounding x exit P/B'. IAG does not compound book: dividend policy is 60-80% of NPAT, plus buybacks ($200m FY26, $443m FY24), and shareholders' equity has been 6.1-7.3bn for ten years (FY16 6,563 -> FY26 7,232). The value is the distributable earnings stream, so the model discounts free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity with net debt at zero, built on the engine so the dashboard reproduces it (same treatment as GMG.AX/CHC.AX operating-earnings streams; memory has no IAG entry, first valuation). A cash-flow DCF is impossible here: the financial-parser could not separate capex from investment-portfolio purchases, and OCF is claims-timing noise. BVPS x EXIT P/B CROSS-CHECK (memo): BVPS 7,232/2,344 = $3.09; ROE 13.9% FY26, 15% ambition; sustainable P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (0.145-0.025)/(0.09-0.025) = 1.85x -> $5.7 on current book, $6.4 with the retained-capital growth path; the base case below ($6-7) is the same answer from the other side. At current_price the market is paying ~2.6x book, ~18x FY26 EPS and ~16.5x base FY27 EPS. ANCHORS: FY26 (30 Jun 2026) NPAT 1,022, NEP 10,523, GWP 18,412, reported margin 14.7%, underlying 15.0% (16.0% ex-RACQI), CET1 1.14x PCA (target 0.9-1.1x), PCA multiple 2.12x (target 1.6-1.8x), DPS 32.0c (74% payout). FY27 guidance: GWP +5-8%, reported margin 14.5-16.5%, perils allowance $1,491m. RAC INSURANCE (WA): ACCC opposed the $1,350m acquisition on 23 Sep 2026 after a Phase 2 review; IAG will lodge a Public Benefit Application. Excluded from base and bear; bull assumes a late, partial WA outcome. Several Ambition 2030 targets ($25bn GWP, 11m customers) assumed RAC completion. FY25 comparatives carry a $270m pre-tax corporate benefit from the COVID-19 business-interruption provision release (the reason FY25 NPAT of 1,359 is not the base). Metrics.csv 'Revenue' is AASB 17 insurance revenue (18,666), not the NEP used here; 'FreeCashFlow' and 'CapEx' are blank by design.
inputs.regulatory_capital_note: 30 Jun 2026: CET1 3,337 (1.14x PCA 2,938), AT1 850, Tier 2 2,028, total 6,215 (2.12x). The equity bridge adds the CET1 above the TOP of the 0.9-1.1x target range ((1.14-1.10) x 2,938 = $118m) as returnable surplus now that the RAC deal it was earmarked for is blocked; the further ~$300m down to the 1.0x midpoint is deliberately not added (perils buffer).

equity_bridge.item: Surplus CET1 above top of 0.9-1.1x PCA target range
equity_bridge.note: (1.14 - 1.10) x PCA 2,938, FY26 AR regulatory capital table (line 10729-10737); earmarked for RAC Insurance, which the ACCC opposed 23 Sep 2026

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 GWP guidance midpoint (5-8%) less the NEP lag; near-term NEP path, not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.8-3.0%) is a third of revenue CAGR (8.7-10.5%): expected for a 60-80% payout insurer that also buys back stock, so book is not the growth anchor. The FY21 base year (NPAT -427 on the COVID-19 BI provision and Asian exit; EPS -0.178) makes the 5-year EPS and FCF CAGRs undefined, and the 3-year DPS CAGR (28.7%) is a recovery from the 15c FY23 trough, not a trend. NEP (7.2-8.1%) and GWP (7.7-8.0%) are the clean series; both are rate-driven (claims inflation pass-through) and are faded toward 2.5% in the projection.
historical_growth.notes: revenue_* on AASB 17 insurance revenue (FY21 12,288 -> FY23 13,838 -> FY26 18,666). fcf_3yr on attributable NPAT (FY23 825 -> FY26 1,022), the numerator of the FCFE flow; reported FCF does not exist for IAG. equity_* on shareholders' equity ex-NCI (FY21 6,246 -> FY23 6,653 -> FY26 7,232). Reported insurance margins over ten years: 14.3, 14.9, 18.3, 16.9, 10.1, ~13 (FY21), ~7 (FY22), 9.6, 15.6, 17.5, 14.7 -- mean ~14%, which anchors the long-run base margin.

base.growth_rationale: NEP growth. FY27 6.0%: GWP guidance 5-8% (midpoint 6.5%) includes ~$300m of extra RACQI months and ~$100m multi-year workers' comp premium, less the ~$150m Honey exit; NEP lags GWP slightly as the RACQI quota share earns through. Then fades from rate-driven mid-single-digit (claims inflation pass-through, ~1-2% volume) to 2.5% terminal by FY35. No RAC Insurance contribution. Implies FY30 GWP ~$22bn, short of the $25bn Ambition 2030 target that assumed RAC.
base.margin_rationale: Attributable pre-tax margin on NEP = insurance margin + SH-funds income - interest - NCI. FY27: reported insurance margin 15.0% (guidance 14.5-16.5%; set below the 15.5% midpoint because natural perils have exceeded allowance in 7 of the last 10 years and FY27 carries no BI release) + 3.6% SH-funds income - 1.8% interest - 2.4% NCI = 14.4%. Insurance margin fades to 14.5% (ten-year mean ~14%, lifted for the expense-ratio gains: 22.6% FY26 vs 23.8% FY25) while SH-funds income falls to ~3.2% of NEP as the funds grow slower than premium; long-run 14.5 + 3.2 - 1.7 - 2.4 = 13.6%. FY27 attributable NPAT ~1,124 (EPS ~48c, +10% on FY26's perils-hit 43.4c).
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at ~1.0x a PCA that is ~28% of NEP: 0.35 x NEP growth. FY27 2.1% of NEP (~$235m, ~21% of NPAT; the balance is the 60-80% dividend plus buybacks), fading to 0.9% at 2.5% terminal growth (~9% of NPAT retained at a ~35% return on tangible equity).

bull.growth_rationale: FY27 at the top of guidance (GWP +8%), then the Public Benefit Application succeeds and RAC Insurance (~$1bn+ GWP) lands late in FY28-29 alongside continued rate hardening and retail volume growth from the multi-brand cross-sell; NEP compounds high-single-digit for three years and the $25bn FY30 GWP ambition is roughly met.
bull.margin_rationale: Insurance margin 16.0% in FY27 (the FY26 ex-RACQI underlying margin, with perils at allowance) held at 16.0% as the cloud/AI programme takes the expense ratio toward 21% and RACQI synergies come through; SH-funds income 3.6% fading to 3.4%, interest -1.8%, NCI -2.4%. Long-run 16.0 + 3.4 - 1.8 - 2.4 = 15.2 -> 15.0. FY27 NPAT ~1,220 (52c).
bull.capex_rationale: Same 0.35 x growth retention rule on the faster path; the RAC purchase price itself ($1.35bn) is assumed funded from Tier 2 and the existing surplus, i.e. outside the organic flow, which is generous to the bull.

bear.growth_rationale: FY27 misses the bottom of guidance (GWP +4-5%, NEP +4%): NZ keeps shrinking in AUD, commercial strata and broker lines stay 'fiercely competitive', the Honey exit and affordability-driven lapses bite, and political pressure on premium increases (Small Business Insurance Inquiry, NZ Treasury review) caps rate. RAC never completes. Growth settles at 2-2.5%, i.e. below claims inflation.
bear.margin_rationale: Insurance margin 13.0% in FY27 (perils ~$200m over allowance again, no reserve releases), 12.5% in FY28 (a large east-coast catastrophe year plus reinsurance repricing), then 13.0% long run -- roughly the ten-year mean including the 7-10% years of FY20-FY23; SH-funds income 3.4% -> 3.3%, interest -1.9%, NCI -2.4%. FY27 NPAT ~925 (39c).
bear.capex_rationale: Higher capital intensity (0.45 x growth): APRA perils-risk charges rise with the allowance and the buyback programme stops, so a larger share of a smaller profit is retained.

scenario_narratives.base: IAG delivers FY27 inside guidance (NEP +6%, reported insurance margin 15.0%, below the 15.5% midpoint because perils usually run over allowance), attributable NPAT recovers to ~$1.12bn as the RACQI book sits inside Group reinsurance for a full year, and premium growth then fades from rate-driven mid-single-digit to 2.5% by FY35. Around 80-90% of profit is distributed (60-80% dividend plus buybacks); the rest funds the regulatory capital that a growing premium base requires. RAC Insurance does not complete. The axes that matter are the perils allowance versus experience, the expense ratio, and investment yields on ~$4.5bn of shareholders' funds.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY27 at the top of guidance with a 16% insurance margin (the ex-RACQI underlying run-rate), the Public Benefit Application clears RAC Insurance in FY28-29, the cloud platform and AI agents cut the expense ratio toward 21%, and rate hardening continues while volumes grow through cross-sell across the multi-brand portfolio. NEP compounds high-single-digit for three years and the FY30 $25bn GWP ambition is roughly met; value is capped at an 18x terminal multiple on free cash to equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY27 comes in below guidance on both growth and margin: another perils overrun, NZ and commercial lines shrinking, affordability politics capping rate, and RAC blocked for good. A large catastrophe year in FY28 pushes the insurance margin to 12.5% and reinsurance repricing holds the long-run margin at 13%. Growth settles at 2-2.5%, buybacks stop, and capital intensity rises with the perils allowance. No solvency question (CET1 1.14x, quota-share protection), so the bear is an earnings-and-multiple case, not a survival case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25%: natural-catastrophe volatility is rated high in the Analysis JSON, FY26 missed on perils, climate is structurally raising the allowance every year, and affordability politics are live. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because its two legs -- a 16% sustained margin and RAC Insurance clearing a Public Benefit Application after a formal ACCC Phase 2 opposition on 23 Sep 2026 -- are both contested, and the bull is the only scenario that still contains RAC. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: IAG is valued on the cash it can actually pay its shareholders: attributable profit after the interest on its capital instruments and after the minority partners' share, less the equity it must retain to keep CET1 at target as premium grows, discounted at a 9% AUD cost of equity with no separate debt deduction. The base case, with the insurance margin settling at its ten-year mean of ~14.5% and growth fading to 2.5%, lands well below the current price; the market is capitalising the FY25 peak margin (17.5%, including a BI provision release) and an Ambition 2030 growth plan that assumed a WA acquisition the ACCC has now opposed. A BVPS x sustainable-P/B cross-check (ROE ~14.5%, CoE 9%, g 2.5% -> ~1.85x book -> ~$6) gives the same answer from the balance-sheet side.
key_risks_to_valuation: Perils experience versus allowance is the single largest swing: each $100m of pre-tax overrun is ~3c of EPS and 0.7pp of margin; the allowance itself ($1,491m FY27) has risen ~16% in two years.
The NCI leakage (RACV's 30% of IMA, RACQ's 10% of RACQI) is charged at a fixed 2.4% of NEP; if IMA outgrows the rest of the Group the leakage rises.
Capital retention is modelled at 0.35 x growth on a 28%-of-NEP PCA; an APRA capital-standard change or a shift toward long-tail lines raises the intensity and cuts FCFE.
Discount rate: the base is terminal-heavy (Gordon at 9%/2.5% binds near the 16x cap); each 1pp on the cost of equity moves the value ~15%.
Investment income on ~$4.5bn of shareholders' funds (28% growth assets) and on technical reserves moves with yields and equity markets; FY26's 4.8% technical-reserve yield was already a headwind.
RAC Insurance: a successful Public Benefit Application is upside not in base or bear; a reverse would matter only through the capital already retained for it, which the bridge treats as returnable.
The 20% Berkshire Hathaway quota share runs to 2029; renewal on worse terms would lower the retained margin.
